critical_findings.finding: Evidence-pointer objects in decision_log/supplemental evidence appear non-compliant with the declared single evidence standard ({artifact_ref, entity_id|null, json_pointer, note}). Current objects include extra keys (e.g., candidate_id, artifact_id, quote) and omit entity_id, which would cause the evidence linter/validator (R10/AT10) to fail or force validators to accept non-standard evidence (breaking determinism and downstream consumption).

closure.closure_target: All canonical artifacts that contain evidence pointers (decision_record, trace_report, review_findings, stage_handoffs, decision_log if canonical) must use exactly the specified evidence-pointer object shape; remove/relocate any extra metadata or formalize a wrapper schema that still preserves the exact evidence-pointer object in a dedicated field.
closure.validator_update_needed: Define an explicit schema for any decision_log-like artifact; ensure evidence-pointer fields validate against the exact object contract and reject supersets.
closure.open_questions: Clarify whether decision_log and supplemental_evaluations are canonical freeze-bundle artifacts; if non-canonical, ensure they are excluded from the evidence-pointer linter scope.

critical_findings.finding: Tool policy for the Review stage denies artifact_write/workspace_write, but the architecture/milestones require reviewers to emit findings artifacts (review_findings.json, integration review_findings.json). This creates an operational contradiction that can either block the workflow (no findings can be produced) or incentivize bypass (writing findings in other stages/roles, violating separation and audit controls).

closure.closure_target: Amend tool policy so reviewers can write findings-only artifacts to an allowlisted canonical type/location (and only that), while still denying patches/code/artifact mutation outside findings. Enforce with role-based output-type allowlists (R22/K10 mitigation).

critical_findings.finding: Parallel-lane completion timing can leak into integration behavior unless deterministic merge ordering is fully specified as a pure function of declared inputs (e.g., lane_id ordering, patchset ids). The plan states “deterministic merge ordering independent of wall-clock completion timing” but does not define the ordering function and conflict-handling normalization, risking non-reproducible integrated states across reruns.

closure.closure_target: Specify an explicit deterministic total order for applying lane patchsets (e.g., sort by lane_id, then patchset sequence number, then artifact_ref lexicographic) and define deterministic conflict handling outcomes (escalate vs abort) with recorded inputs/thresholds so reruns produce identical results.
closure.open_questions: Q9 conflict resolution strategy details are blocking for determinism.

critical_findings.finding: artifact_ref naming/versioning/identity semantics are unspecified (blocking Q3). Without a canonical artifact_ref scheme (and hashing/provenance rules), evidence pointers may not be resolvable or may be ambiguously resolvable, undermining audit spine integrity and trace validation.

closure.closure_target: Define artifact_ref format as a stable, content-addressed and/or version-addressed identifier with collision resistance, immutability semantics, and resolver behavior; update validators to require uniqueness + hash binding in run_manifest/event_log.

critical_findings.finding: Diff format and deterministic patch-application normalization are unresolved (blocking Q7; low-confidence A10). In a parallel-lane architecture, this can produce inconsistent patch applies (whitespace/eol normalization, rename handling, file mode changes), non-deterministic conflict surfaces, and divergent repo_snapshots.

closure.closure_target: Choose one patchset diff encoding and specify canonical normalization (line endings, file modes, rename semantics, context lines) plus deterministic apply rules and failure modes; require base_commit in each patchset and verify repo state hash before apply.

critical_findings.finding: Context-pack bounds/selection/adequacy remain underspecified and low-confidence (A11; blocking Q15). In O2, under-selection can cause incorrect lane implementations and late integration failures; over-selection can exceed model context limits, causing truncation and non-deterministic behavior.

closure.closure_target: Define deterministic context-pack selection rules and hard size budgets per role/stage; add a validator that checks required artifact sets are included for each stage/role and that packs are within bounds; define a deterministic summarization/compaction artifact when workspace grows.

critical_findings.finding: Secrets policy requires “validated before any artifact is persisted,” but the plan mainly specifies checkpoint/boundary scans. With artifact_write allowed in Generate/WorkPlanning and append-only logs, a secret can be durably written before detection unless writes are mediated by a synchronous pre-write scanner/redactor at the storage/workspace gateway.

closure.closure_target: Make secrets scanning/redaction a mandatory pre-write gate in the artifact/workspace write path (not only at checkpoints), including event-log append operations; ensure scanner outputs do not echo secrets; define deterministic blocking behavior and remediation steps.
closure.warnings: If the system cannot guarantee pre-persistence scanning (e.g., third-party log sinks), the design must explicitly accept residual leakage risk or prohibit those sinks.

critical_findings.finding: Network is deny-by-default across stages, but dependency installation/build/test often requires package-manager network access. Blocking Q11 leaves a high likelihood of systematic validation failures or ad-hoc permission expansions (which can be non-deterministic and risky), undermining reproducibility and supply-chain controls.

closure.closure_target: Define a deterministic dependency/network policy: offline mirrors or allowlisted registries, lockfile enforcement, caching strategy, and how/when network can be enabled with provenance recorded; incorporate dependency/SBOM validators into quality_reports/release_bundle.
